title: assess-serving-preemption
summary: Assess whether LLM serving queue delays justify token-boundary priority preemption, accounting for suspended KV, host swapping or recomputation, and long-request service guarantees. Use for admission-versus-service-order diagnosis, not current scheduler implementation or tenant-fairness certification.

skill_metadata.name: assess-serving-preemption
skill_metadata.description: Assess whether LLM serving queue delays justify token-boundary priority preemption, accounting for suspended KV, host swapping or recomputation, and long-request service guarantees. Use for admission-versus-service-order diagnosis, not current scheduler implementation or tenant-fairness certification.

applicability.scope: Diagnosing whether LLM serving queue delay justifies token-boundary priority preemption, including suspended KV, host swap or recomputation and long-request service guarantees; admission-versus-service-order diagnosis, not current scheduler implementation or tenant-fairness certification
applicability.prerequisites: The packaged source notes are read before quoting a metric or comparing a baseline; installing, benchmarking, changing scheduling or admission, migrating state, editing a repository or running a reproduction needs a separately authorized task
applicability.input_contract: The late boundary (first token, token gap, completion or a stated cohort's service) with its exact percentile or attainment target and denominator; model and KV format, engine revision, safe interruption boundary, request batch limit, input/output/context distributions, arrival bursts, device live/reserved/allocated bytes, active and suspended requests, host budget, transfer path, recovery time and queue/phase/service timings; per-tenant or priority-class obligations kept apart from aggregate latency
applicability.produced_artifact: A read-only decision naming the observed failure boundary, the smallest candidate that addresses it, unchanged assumptions, missing evidence, resource cost, affected cohorts, counter-signal and next authorized gate, plus a proposed verification plan; not a validated configuration
failure_modes: An ordinary iteration boundary is taken to permit interrupting a prefill halfway through
Unknown output length is treated as known from the prompt
KV is counted for the running batch only, omitting started requests that are suspended
Reservations are removed because some reserved capacity is not live
Recompute-based eviction is proposed without a progress invariant, so two jobs can repeatedly displace each other
Host-device copies or same-host IPC are charged to Network instead of their local resource
applicability.refusal_point: Withholds a preemption recommendation when the apparent gain can be explained by different kernels, unmatched parallelism or an incomparable latency metric; unknown safe boundaries, unsupported state recovery, uncalibrated timing or unclear service obligations are blockers

recommendations: Name the late boundary and its exact target and denominator before choosing among batching, admission, preemption and state recovery.

Send prefill interference to choose-prefill-decode-schedule and physical KV slack to diagnose-kv-block-efficiency when those candidates are available; otherwise report the diagnosed boundary and the missing evidence.
In a later authorized test, isolate service ordering first and state recovery second, and evaluate their interaction only after both are understood.
Weigh FastServe's same-engine FCFS comparison above its historical-vLLM headline, and do not read its P95 aggregate gain as a starvation or tenant-fairness guarantee.
limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.
